items.series: T-PLUS P2 It really happened, on the clock
items.hypothesis: TP-B1 P2: DOCUMENTARY_STORY on the live clock; primary = public views at 48 h.
items.caption:
CGI reconstruction, not footage. 66 million years ago, an asteroid ~10–15 km wide hit what is now Mexico. Its first day, on the clock.
A ~200 km crater in minutes; by the end of the day ~130 m of rock inside it, sealed by tsunami sand full of charcoal. Textures: Solar System Scope. Moon photo: NASA.

items.series: T-PLUS P1 What if, on the clock
items.hypothesis: TP-B1 P1: MODEL on the T+ clock; primary = public views at 48 h.
items.caption:
What if the Moon just vanished? You'd still see it for 1.3 seconds.
Then the biggest tides shrink to about a third, and over millions of years Earth's tilt could swing up to 85°. A thought experiment. Photos: NASA. Textures: Solar System Scope.
